subject.title: fix: stabilize OpenClaw beta setup and PT-PT formatting

question: Should the Windows Companion make OpenClaw `2026.7.2-beta.3` its default before an official artifact containing the upstream wizard-runtime correction has passed the real setup path?
rationale: The branch deliberately changes the supported install default, while the documented passing run uses an unmerged external dependency and the official artifact still fails; selecting a prerelease and accepting that dependency boundary requires maintainer release-policy intent.

options.title: Wait for an official proven artifact
options.body: Keep the lifecycle fixes but defer the default-version change until an official release contains the upstream correction and exact-head setup/reconnect evidence passes without injection.

options.title: Accept beta.3 as an explicit temporary default
options.body: Merge with a maintainer-owned release note and support plan acknowledging that the default artifact still cannot complete the native-wizard setup path.

options.title: Split the version selection
options.body: Land the bounded Companion fixes separately and leave the existing default pin until the upstream artifact is available.

recommendation.title: Wait for an official proven artifact
recommendation.body: Keep the lifecycle fixes but defer the default-version change until an official release contains the upstream correction and exact-head setup/reconnect evidence passes without injection.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history connects CassieMei most closely to the affected setup/version path, though the final release-policy choice should be confirmed by a repository decision-maker.
